Saves the sound card's volume levels on shutdown and restores them on boot (at the ALSA level, below PipeWire). Disabling it means volume resets to a default value on every boot.
Auto-nice: automatically adjusts the priority of known processes (e.g. lowers miners/compilers, raises games) based on rules. Safe to disable, everything reverts to normal priority.
Device discovery on the local network (mDNS/Zeroconf -- printers, Chromecast, etc. that "just show up"). Safe to disable if you don't use that kind of device.
Manages the Bluetooth adapter (pairing, connecting headphones/mouse/etc). Required for any Bluetooth device -- safe to disable if you don't use any.
CoolerControl daemon -- fan/liquid cooling control. Disabling it leaves fans on their factory (BIOS) curve, without the custom profile.
The system D-Bus message bus -- the communication infrastructure between almost every Linux service. Critical, do not touch.
Text console (TTY login, e.g. Ctrl+Alt+F2) -- one instance per virtual terminal. This is a "template" unit (the @ is a parameter), it doesn't activate on its own without a real TTY behind it.
Creates static device nodes for kernel modules that need them before udev starts. Do not touch.
Syncs the Limine bootloader's boot entries with Snapper snapshots (btrfs). Only relevant if you use system snapshots -- don't touch it if you don't know what Snapper is.
Monitors LVM volumes (mirrors, snapshots) if the machine uses LVM for disks. If you don't use LVM, it doesn't do anything useful but doesn't get in the way either.
Microsoft SQL Server database engine (the sqlservr process you see in the Processes tab). Can be disabled without affecting the rest of the system if you don't use a local SQL Server database.
Manages all network connections (WiFi, Ethernet, VPN) -- what nmcli/the network applet uses. Disabling it leaves the machine without managed networking.
Runs custom scripts when the network state changes (connect/disconnect). With no scripts of your own in /etc/NetworkManager/dispatcher.d/, it doesn't do anything visible.
Delays services that depend on the network until NetworkManager confirms there's a real connection at boot. Safe to disable if you don't mind some service starting "before" it has network.
Closes the boot splash screen (Plymouth) once boot has finished. Part of the same mechanism.
Keeps the boot splash screen visible until the rest of boot has actually finished (avoids a flash of an empty console). Part of the same mechanism.
Tells Plymouth the disk is now mounted read-write, so it can save data if needed. Part of the same boot mechanism.
Shows the boot splash screen during startup, before reaching login. Disabling it shows raw boot text instead of the splash.

Authorization agent (PolicyKit) -- what shows the "administrator password" dialogs for individual actions (pkexec). Critical: without this, panels like this dashboard's Firewall/Services can no longer request permissions.
Power profiles (performance/balanced/power saver) -- what the GNOME/KDE power applet switches between. Safe to disable if you don't use those profiles.
The display manager -- the graphical login screen that starts the Hyprland session. Critical: disabling it leaves no graphical way to log in.
The systemd-boot variant of the above -- saves the random seed on the EFI partition. Do not touch.
Flushes logs held in memory to persistent disk storage at boot. Do not touch.
Collects and stores system logs (what journalctl reads from). Critical -- can't be disabled without breaking the event log.
Handles user sessions, login, and power buttons (suspend/shutdown from the keyboard). Critical for any graphical session.
Loads the kernel modules listed in /etc/modules-load.d/ at boot. Do not touch.
Saves/restores the random number generator's seed across reboots. Do not touch.
Remounts the root and kernel filesystems with their final permissions during boot. Runs only once at boot, do not touch.
Resolves domain names (DNS) for the system. Disabling it can leave the machine unable to resolve web addresses.
Applies the kernel parameters (sysctl) defined in /etc/sysctl.d/ at boot. Do not touch.
Syncs the system clock via NTP. Safe to disable if you use another NTP client, otherwise the clock can drift out of sync.
Creates/cleans up temporary files and directories defined by systemd and packages at boot (e.g. /tmp, /run). Do not touch.
Variant of the above, specific to device nodes in /dev. Do not touch.
Early version (before /dev is fully populated) of the above. Do not touch.
Loads udev rules passed in as credentials (a boot mechanism, uncommon outside containers/VMs). Do not touch.
Forces udev to re-detect all hardware already connected at boot ("coldplug"). Do not touch.
Detects new hardware (USB, disks, etc.) and creates their device nodes in /dev. Critical -- without this, hot-plugged devices don't show up.
Logs system startup/shutdown events to UTMP (what commands like `who`/`last` use). Do not touch.
Enables regular user logins after boot (blocks logins while the system is still starting up). Do not touch.
Loads user/group records passed in as credentials at boot. Do not touch.
Serves user/group records in JSON format to other systemd services (part of the identity infrastructure, not an app). Do not touch.
Configures the keyboard layout and font for the virtual console (TTY) at boot. Do not touch.
Manages mounting/unmounting removable disks (USB, etc.) without privileges -- what the file manager uses to mount a flash drive. Don't disable if you mount disks from the UI.
The UFW firewall (managed from the dashboard's Network -> Firewall tab). Disabling it turns off packet filtering entirely.
Reports battery/power status to other apps (battery indicators, etc.). Doesn't do much on a desktop without a battery, but doesn't hurt to leave it on.
Handles WiFi authentication (WPA/WPA2/WPA3) -- NetworkManager depends on this to connect to wireless networks. Don't disable if you use WiFi.
